IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA  CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION  CIVIL APPEAL NO.7304 OF 2024  (Arising out of SLP(Civil) No. 17392/2023)
 BASHIR AHMAD BHAT   VERSUS  STATE OF JAMMU AND KASHMIR & ORS. 
 O R D E R 1.
Leave granted.

2. This appeal is filed against the judgment dated 10.11.2022 of the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh at Srinagar in OWP No.113/2014, whereby the appellant has been awarded compensation for the acquired land after determining its market value as on the date when Section 6 notification was issued on 09.08.2007.
3.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The controversy in this case is regarding the cut- off date for the determination of market value.
4. It may be mentioned that the land of the appellant was acquired by following the procedure contemplated under the Jammu & Kashmir State Land Acquisition Act, 1990 (in short, the Act).

entities.text: Jammu & Kashmir State Land Acquisition Act, 1990
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Section 23 of the Act provides factors to be considered in determining compensation, the first consideration amongst which is the market value of acquired land on the date of the Section 6 Declaration under the Act.

Section 23 of the Act reads as follows:

sentences.text: Matters to be considered in determining compensation

(2) In addition to the market value of the land as above provided, the Court shall in every case award a sum of fifteen per centum on such market value in consideration of the compulsory nature of the acquisition.
5. It is a matter of record that a corrigendum to include the appellants land under Section 6 of the Act was issued on 30.07.2012.
However, the compensation awarded to the appellant is based on the premise that the original notification under Section 6 in respect of the adjoining lands came to be issued on 09.08.2007.
6. It thus seems to us that the controversy can be given quietus by granting a reasonable annual escalation of not more than 12% to the appellant from 2008 to 2012.
7. Consequently, the appeal is allowed in part.

The impugned judgment of the High Court is modified and the appellant is held entitled to the additional annual escalation at the rate of 12% for the years 2008 to 2012, besides other statutory benefits.
Let the amount of compensation payable to the appellant be accordingly recalculated and be released within a period of 10 weeks.

8. It is clarified that since the appellants land was included in the acquisition process by way of corrigendum, the aforesaid directions are being issued in the peculiar facts and circumstances of Bashir Ahmad Bhat vs State Of Jammu And Kashmir on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194330894/
